name: Last Visited MRU
purpose: Tracks which applications the user has run through a standard Open/Save dialog and the last folder location each application interacted with.
key_fields: MRUListEx - binary DWORD-array giving the order entries were used, most recent first
Value data - the executable name of the application that opened the dialog, paired with a binary PIDL (Win7+) or plain path (XP) for the last-used folder
Key LastWrite time - approximates when the most recent entry was recorded
normal_baseline: Entries for common applications (Office, PDF readers, browsers) paired with everyday working folders (Documents, Desktop, project directories) the user regularly accesses.
anomalies: An application paired with a folder location the user has no business reason to access, including other users' profiles or administrative shares
A folder path referencing a hidden, obfuscated, or unusually named directory (dotted or random-character names) used as a working/staging location
Applications commonly used for malicious purposes (archive tools, scripting hosts) appearing paired with folder locations tied to sensitive data
Entries pointing to a removable/external drive letter not otherwise associated with that user's normal workflow
anti_forensic_notes: Like other ComDlg32 MRU keys, entries are only written once the dialog interaction completes, so activity in a dialog left open (or a process killed before the dialog closes) may not be captured. Entries persist after the referenced folder is renamed or deleted, so the recorded path can outlive the location it names.
interpretation: This key yields two distinct pieces of evidence in one place: which applications the user actually ran through a file dialog, and the last filesystem location each application touched - not necessarily the same as where the current file resides. Because the PIDL/path often points at directories with no other UI presence, this is a common source for identifying hidden or otherwise-unadvertised directories the user (or a GUI-driven malicious application) has visited.
